title: CEO drop-in — dataplane privacy Q&A (scratch)
body:
Purpose:
Short scratch to frame the CEO 10–12 minute drop-in on 'dataplane privacy' for the all-hands. This is a working list of top-lines, likely questions, and suggested language. Use as a crib sheet for rapid answers and to flag open items to follow up after the town hall.

TL;DR (one-liner the CEO can say):
We treat customer data in the dataplane as sacred — we minimize exposure, encrypt in transit and at rest, give customers control via keys and private deployments, and we continue to invest in auditability and tooling so teams can run critical workloads with confidence.

Opening 60–90s (notes to CEO):
- Quick acknowledgement of why privacy comes up now (recent RFPs, a few customers asking for air-gapped options).
- Reassure: we have clear controls across Hosted / Dedicated / Private, and a roadmap to tighten telemetry and access.
- Close: follow-up Q&A and post-all-hands writeup planned; encourage product/security folks to post more detail in Confluence.

Key talking points (short bullets):
- Customers can choose the deployment mode that matches their compliance needs: Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (isolation & SLA), Private (VPC/on-prem with customer KMS).
- Data minimization principle: we do not persist customer prompt/output beyond short-lived caching windows unless explicitly opted-in for debugging/billing.
- Encryption: TLS in transit + AES-256 at rest for hosted metadata; customer KMS/HSM integrations for Private.
- Access controls & audits: RBAC for internal tools, strict break-glass, and audit logs with retention controls per contract.
- Industry compliance: SOC2 + underway work for ISO27001 and targeted FedRAMP conversations for specific customers (status: exploratory).
- Continuous improvements: investing in telemetry filtering, tokenization options, and easier customer-facing privacy toggles in Console.

Likely Qs and suggested succinct answers (prep for follow-ups):
1) Q: Are customer prompts used to train models?
   A: No. We do not use customer prompt or output data to train or fine-tune models unless the customer explicitly opts in. We clearly surface this in contracts and Console toggles.

2) Q: What happens if there’s a data leak?
   A: We have an incident playbook and SLAs for notification. For Dedicated/Private customers we provide tailored runbooks and we’ll prioritize containment and support. We’ll follow up with affected customers and regulators as required.

3) Q: Can we support FIPS / HSM workflows?
   A: Yes — Private deployments already support KMS integrations; roadmap includes tighter HSM/FIPS guidance and partner validation (ETA: next quarter for published guide).

4) Q: How much of this is configurable by customers?
   A: A lot — you can choose model variants, retention windows, KMS key usage, and private deployment for full control. We’re working on more self-serve toggles in Console to make this easier.

5) Q: Do we log full inputs/outputs for debugging?
   A: By default we capture limited telemetry for performance and billing. Full logs are only captured with explicit customer consent or under support debug sessions with strict controls and retention limits.

Tone guidance for answers: calm, concrete, avoid overpromising specifics if still in roadmap. For any item that is 'on the roadmap' say timeframe ranges (e.g., Q2, next quarter) not exact dates.

Open items / dark corners to flag after the drop-in (notes for follow-up owners):
- Clarify official retention windows and make them visible in Console (owner: Product + Security; ping Samir).
- Draft a short post-all-hands FAQ doc that links to Confluence PRIV playbook (owner: comms + Kyra).
- Finalize HSM/FIPS partner list and put 'validation' status on product page (owner: infra-security).
- Confirm exact language for contract addendum re: training-data usage and sync with Legal (owner: Legal; ticket PRIV-42).
- Quick audit of all telemetry pipelines to ensure PII/moonshot tokens are filtered before logs land in analytics (owner: Observability).

Practical rehearsal notes (for the CEO):
- Expect 2–3 live questions; have 3 canned answers ready (training-data, logs, private deployments).
- If asked for a detailed whitepaper, say: "Yes — we'll publish a short technical brief within 2 weeks and a longer compliance pack in collaboration with Legal."
- Keep bridging back to customer control and the product choices they can make today.

Slack/Comms cues post-all-hands (quick checklist):
- Post a 3–4 line summary in #company-announcements linking Confluence brief (owner: Kyra).
- Ping #security-ops and #solutions-eng for any incoming customer threads to triage.
- Open a Confluence 'TownHall privacy FAQ' page and tag product/security owners, set 7-day draft deadline.

Quick escalation map (who to call in first 30 minutes if a customer press inquiry happens):
- On-call Legal: Marta Chen
- Security lead: Samir Alvarez
- Head of Product: [TBD — name placeholder] (note: reach out to Karim for confirmation)

Loose crumbs / scratch ideas (stream-of-consciousness — keep):
- Could we add a small toggle in Console for 'minimal telemetry' that is default for enterprise trials?
- Prepare one pager for sales with differentiated language for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private re: privacy guarantees.
- Consider a webinar for customers focused on 'deploying Redwood with sensitive data' — coordinate with Solutions Eng.

To-dos (next 72h):
- Finalize and send the post-all-hands FAQ draft (Kyra).
- Confirm Head of Product name for escalation (Kyra / Samir).
- Draft the one-paragraph CEO script and get quick approval (Samir + Marta).

-- end scratch --

Notes to self: keep this informal, expect edits; will convert to Confluence canonical copy after the all-hands. Replace placeholders before publishing.
